correctness.rationale: The target-input density identity follows exactly by conditioning on the binary response mode and rewriting the tilted mode weights through \(q_b\). Holding \(p\) fixed makes the intercept an even smooth function of \(\eta\), giving \(s_\eta(v)=3\eta v+O(\eta^2)\) uniformly. Centering cancels the first KL term, yielding the stated \(3/2\) coefficient; differentiating the exact density yields the Fisher coefficient. The triangular likelihood ratio has bounded vanishing increments, the displayed mean and variance, and therefore satisfies Lindeberg. Pinsker and a bounded sample-mean test establish the two outer regimes. The packaged deterministic quadrature independently replays the leading constants for the motivating source normalization.

value.rationale: The source paper explicitly uses \(\eta\) as a sensitivity axis and observes severe estimator instability before the exact nonidentification point. Quantifying the transition by \(m\eta^2\) turns that qualitative ladder into an interpretable sample-size law, gives exact information and testing constants, and separates unavoidable information loss from estimator-specific failure. This is a natural boundary of the motivating model rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
